knowledge:
- key_parameters: trylist=A list of lists, where each sublist contains 'exprs' (a matrix of genomic data with genes as rows and samples as columns) and 'classlab' (a 0/1 vector indicating control/normal as 0 and tumor/case as 1) ;; side=A character vector specifying the direction of outlier detection ("up" for over-expression/amplification, "down" for under-expression/hypo-methylation) for each study in the input list ;; type=A character string, either "subtype" (to find genes outlier-expressed in a subset of samples in at least one study) or "uniform" (to find genes consistently outlier-expressed across all studies) ;; topcut=An integer specifying how many top-ranked genes to plot in PlotTopPCOPA ;; TopGeneNum=An integer specifying the number of top PCOPA-scored genes to consider when generating patient-specific outlier gene lists
- alternatives: limma and SAM (preferred when genes differ statistically across the majority of tumor samples rather than a subset); COPA, Outlier Sums, and Wu's statistic (alternative outlier detection statistics for single datasets, whereas coGPS is preferred for multi-study/multi-platform integration and gene set analysis)
- when_to_use: When analyzing multi-platform genomic data (e.g., matched expression, methylation, and copy number variation) or multiple independent studies of the same biological process to identify cancer outlier genes (disregulated in only a subset of tumor samples) and perform downstream gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA)
- pitfalls: Sample ordering is critical for patient-specific outlier gene list generation; if using PatientSpecificGeneList, the samples in each data type must be in the exact same order (i.e., column j in all matrices must represent the same patient). If only calculating PCOPA scores or running GSEA, sample matching across data types is not strictly required. Additionally, 'exprs' must be a matrix (not a data frame) with row names (gene names) and column names (sample names), and 'classlab' must be a vector (not a list or data frame).

workflows.name: outlier_detection_and_gsea
workflows.intent: Identify outlier genes across multiple genomic datasets using PCOPA, calculate permutation-based p-values, visualize top results, and perform gene set enrichment analysis.
input: cnv.csv (matrix of copy number variation values)
class_labels.csv (binary vectors indicating normal/tumor status for each dataset)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare input list of matrices and class labels ;; 2. Run PCOPA to calculate outlier statistics (subtype or uniform) ;; 3. Plot top-ranked outlier genes using PlotTopPCOPA ;; 4. Run permutation tests using permCOPA to calculate p-values ;; 5. Perform downstream gene set enrichment analysis using Wilcoxon rank sum test (wilcoxGST from limma)
workflows.code:
Exon_exprs<-as.matrix(Exon_exprs_matched)
Methy_exprs<-as.matrix(Methy_exprs_matched)
CNV_exprs<-as.matrix(CNV_exprs_matched)
Exon_classlab<-unlist(Exon_classlab_matched)
Methy_classlab<-unlist(Methy_classlab_matched)
CNV_classlab<-unlist(CNV_classlab_matched)
trylist<-list()
trylist[[1]]<-list(exprs=Exon_exprs,classlab=Exon_classlab)
trylist[[2]]<-list(exprs=Methy_exprs,classlab=Methy_classlab)
trylist[[3]]<-list(exprs=CNV_exprs,classlab=CNV_classlab)
a7<-PCOPA(trylist,0.05,side=c("up","down","up"),type="subtype")
a8<-PCOPA(trylist,0.05,side=c("up","down","up"),type="uniform")
PlotTopPCOPA(trylist,a8,topcut=1,typelist=c("Exon","Methy","CNV"))
perma7<-permCOPA(trylist,0.05,side=c("up","down","up"),type="subtype",perms=2)
pvaluea7<-sapply(1:length(a7),function(i) 
	length(which(perma7[i,]>a7[i]))/ncol(perma7))
dista7<-as.vector(perma7)
pvaluea7<-sapply(1:length(a7),function(i) 
	length(which(dista7>a7[i]))/length(dista7))
library(limma)
data(human_c1)
genename<-rownames(Exon_exprs)
test_set1_a7<-rep(1,length(Hs.gmtl.c1))
for(i in 1:length(Hs.gmtl.c1))
{
	set<-Hs.gmtl.c1[[i]]
 	matched<-match(genename,set)
	index<-is.na(matched)==FALSE
	if(sum(as.numeric(index))>0)
	{
		test_set1_a7[i]<-wilcoxGST(index,a7)
	}
	else
	{
		test_set1_a7[i]<-NA
	}
}

workflows.name: patient_specific_outlier_lists
workflows.intent: Generate patient-specific outlier gene lists for clinical settings where samples across different data types are matched and ordered identically.
input: matched_gene_expression.csv (matrix of gene expression values with matched sample ordering)
matched_methylation.csv (matrix of methylation values with matched sample ordering)
matched_cnv.csv (matrix of copy number variation values with matched sample ordering)
class_labels.csv (binary vectors indicating normal/tumor status for each dataset)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare matched and identically ordered input list of matrices and class labels ;; 2. Run PatientSpecificGeneList to extract outlier genes for each individual patient ;; 3. Retrieve the outlier gene list for specific patients
workflows.code:
Exon_exprs<-as.matrix(Exon_exprs_matched)
Methy_exprs<-as.matrix(Methy_exprs_matched)
CNV_exprs<-as.matrix(CNV_exprs_matched)
Exon_classlab<-unlist(Exon_classlab_matched)
Methy_classlab<-unlist(Methy_classlab_matched)
CNV_classlab<-unlist(CNV_classlab_matched)
trylist<-list()
trylist[[1]]<-list(exprs=Exon_exprs,classlab=Exon_classlab)
trylist[[2]]<-list(exprs=Methy_exprs,classlab=Methy_classlab)
trylist[[3]]<-list(exprs=CNV_exprs,classlab=CNV_classlab)
IndividualList7<-PatientSpecificGeneList(trylist,0.05,side=c("down","up","down"),
type="subtype",TopGeneNum=100)
